content: 1. Lercher et al. (2011) conducted research in Austria to investigate the cardiovascular effects of environmental noise, publishing their findings in the journal Noise & Health. 2. In 2010, Lercher and colleagues examined the impact of railway noise on the use of sleep medication, presenting results from the ALPNAP study in Noise & Health. 3. Lercher et al. (2008) explored the health effects and key contributing factors associated with exposure to rail and road noise along transalpine traffic corridors. Their findings were presented at the 9th International Congress on Noise as a Public Health Problem (ICBEN 2008) in the USA. 4. Lercher et al. (2013) investigated the relationship between traffic noise exposure and disturbed sleep in children living in alpine valleys. This study was presented at the 42nd International Congress on Noise Control Engineering (INTER-NOISE 2013) in Innsbruck, Austria. 5. Lercher, Evans, and Meis (2003) studied the effects of ambient noise on cognitive processes in primary school children, with their findings published in Environment and Behavior. 6. Levesque et al. (2010) assessed the exposure of high school students in Québec City, Canada, to noise from personal music players, publishing their results in the International Journal of Child and Adolescent Health. 7. Lopez et al. (2006) edited a comprehensive report on the global burden of disease and risk factors, published by the World Bank and Oxford University Press. 8. Liu et al. (2014) examined the associations between traffic-related air pollution, noise, and blood pressure in children, using data from the GINIplus and LISAplus studies, published in the International Journal of Hygiene and Environmental Health. 9. Liu et al. (2013) investigated the relationship between road traffic noise exposure and blood pressure in German children, with findings published in Noise & Health. 10. Locher et al. (2018) analyzed differences in outdoor and indoor sound levels based on window positions (open, tilted, or closed), publishing their results in the International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health. 11. Lukas et al. (1981) reported on the effects of freeway noise on the academic achievement of elementary school children and proposed a criterion level for school noise abatement programs, in a study commissioned by the California Department of Health Services. 12. Maassen et al. (2001) investigated ear damage caused by leisure noise, with their findings published in Noise & Health. 13. Martin et al. (2013) conducted a randomized trial to evaluate interventions for preventing noise-induced hearing loss and tinnitus in children, publishing their results in the International Journal of Audiology. 14. Maschke (2003) presented epidemiological research on the stress caused by traffic noise and its effects on high blood pressure and psychological disturbances at the 8th International Congress on Noise as a Public Health Problem (ICBEN 2003) in Rotterdam, Netherlands. 15. Maschke and Hecht (2005) explored the pathogenesis mechanisms of noise-induced clinical conditions, drawing lessons from the Spandau Health Survey, published in Umweltmedizin in Forschung und Praxis. 16. Maschke et al. (2003) examined the influence of noise stress on the immune system and the development of arteriosclerosis, with findings published by the Umweltbundesamt in Berlin. 17. Mathers et al. (2003) provided a detailed analysis of the global burden of disease in 2002, including data sources, methods, and results, in a report by the World Health Organization. 18. Mathers, Vos, and Stevenson (1999) assessed the burden of disease and injury in Australia, publishing their findings through the Australian Institute of Health and Welfare. 19. Matheson et al. (2010) studied the effects of road traffic and aircraft noise exposure on children’s episodic memory as part of the RANCH project, with results published in Noise & Health. 20. Matsui (2013) investigated psychosomatic disorders caused by aircraft noise and their causal pathways, presenting findings at the 42nd International Congress on Noise Control Engineering (INTER-NOISE 2013) in Innsbruck, Austria. 21. Matsui et al. (2004) examined the effects of chronic aircraft noise on blood pressure and psychological indices in the Okinawa study, publishing their findings in the Journal of Sound and Vibration. 22. McCunney et al. (2014) critically reviewed the scientific literature on wind turbines and health, publishing their findings in the Journal of Occupational and Environmental Medicine. 23. Michaud (2015) assessed outcomes related to wind turbine noise and health in the Health Canada study, presenting results at the 44th International Congress on Noise Control Engineering (INTER-NOISE 2015) in San Francisco, USA. 24. Miedema and Oudshoorn (2001) analyzed the relationship between transportation noise annoyance and exposure metrics, publishing their findings in Environmental Health Perspectives. 25. Moehler et al. (1997) evaluated the effects of railway noise reduction on annoyance after rail-grinding, presenting their findings at the 26th International Congress on Noise Control Engineering (INTER-NOISE 1997) in Budapest, Hungary. 26. Morgan et al. (2016) applied the GRADE framework to assess the quality of evidence in environmental and occupational health, publishing their findings in Environment International. 27. Morrell et al. (1998) examined the cross-sectional relationship between blood pressure in schoolchildren and aircraft noise, presenting findings at the 7th International Congress on Noise as a Public Health Problem (ICBEN 1998) in Sydney, Australia. 28. Morrell et al. (2000) conducted a follow-up study on child blood pressure and aircraft noise, presenting results at the 29th International Congress on Noise Control Engineering (INTER-NOISE 2000) in Nice, France. 29. Murray (1994) quantified the burden of disease using disability-adjusted life years (DALYs), publishing the technical basis in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization. 30. Murray and Acharya (1997) provided an in-depth explanation of DALYs in the Journal of Health Economics. 31. Murray and Lopez (2013) measured the global burden of disease, publishing their findings in the New England Journal of Medicine. 32. Neitzel and Fligor (2017) reviewed the risk of noise-induced hearing loss from recreational sound exposure, publishing their findings in a report accessible online. 33. Nguyen et al. (2015) conducted social surveys around Noi Bai Airport before and after the opening of a new terminal, presenting findings at the 44th International Congress on Noise Control Engineering (INTER-NOISE 2015) in San Francisco, USA. 34. Nguyen et al. (2012) compared models predicting annoyance from combined noise in Ho Chi Minh City and Hanoi, publishing their findings in Applied Acoustics. 35. Nguyen et al. (2010) studied community responses to aircraft and combined noises in Hanoi, presenting findings at the 39th International Congress on Noise Control Engineering (INTER-NOISE 2010) in Lisbon, Portugal. 36. Nieuwenhuijsen et al. (2017) systematically reviewed the effects of environmental noise on adverse birth outcomes, publishing their findings in the International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health. 37. Nilsson and Berglund (2006) examined noise annoyance and activity disturbance before and after the erection of a roadside noise barrier, publishing their findings in the Journal of the Acoustical Society of America. 38. Notley et al. (2014) summarized findings from the National Noise Attitude Survey 2012 (NNAS 2012), publishing a report accessible online. 39. Oehrstroem et al. (2004) conducted longitudinal surveys on the effects of road traffic noise on sleep, using wrist actigraphs and sleep logs, publishing their findings in the Journal of Sound and Vibration. 40. Oftedal et al. (2014) investigated the relationship between traffic noise and markers of obesity in a population-based study, presenting findings at the 11th International Congress on Noise as a Public Health Problem (ICBEN 2014) in Nara, Japan. 41. Pedersen (2011) examined health aspects associated with wind turbine noise, publishing results from three field studies in the Noise Control Engineering Journal. 42. Pedersen and Persson Waye (2004) analyzed the perception and annoyance caused by wind turbine noise, establishing a dose-response relationship, published in the Journal of the Acoustical Society of America.
